verdict.rationale: Glama hosts registry servers on its own infrastructure and returns a Gateway endpoint URL that MCP clients connect to. Calls through that URL reach the server's tools, and Glama manages logging, access control and credentials. Pre-filled config blocks for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code and VS Code make pointing a client at the server copy-and-paste. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting a client to a Glama-hosted URL, and explicit documentation of the hosted endpoint's transport (Streamable HTTP/SSE) and client auth flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can point my MCP-compatible client at a hosted remote server URL and reach downstream tools without deploying any infrastructure

citations.quote: Deploy any server from the registry to Glama and we automatically put the Gateway in front of it. No proxy setup, no manual wiring – the endpoint you get is the Gateway.
Every call through this URL is logged, access-controlled, and credential-managed
each server page shows the exact JSON block to paste, pre-filled for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and VS Code
Every MCP call from your agents flows through Glama
